body: [{"streamId":"01a0c45a-f144-7207-96c8-3cdff53fecfd","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskAdded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0c45a-f144-7207-96c8-3cdff53fecfd\u0022,\u0022ProjectId\u0022:\u002201a077d8-2b7d-75a0-a0eb-c3deff5f2a4e\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:\u0022A node already vouched under the owner root on one project ledger joins a new project on its own: it establishes that root on the new ledger with its vouch carried as signed evidence, takes the genesis member slot with a fresh project key, and comes out verified there without the root-holding node ever touching the project\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022h9k project join \\u003Cproject\\u003E on a node whose own key is enrolled under owner root R on another project ledger this install has registered (found by reading each registered project chain; --from-project \\u003Cname\\u003E names one explicitly) and whose target ledger has no root for R writes, in one push: owners/R/root.yaml as a verbatim copy of the source ledger root file, and owners/R/carried/\\u003Cnode-id\\u003E.yaml holding the source root.yaml, the source vouch owners/R/nodes/\\u003Cnode-id\\u003E.yaml, the raw bytes of both signed commits, and provenance (source project id and key, origin URL, commit SHAs), signed with this node key. It is refused with one plain sentence when no source vouch exists, when this node key is revoked on the source, or when the target already has a root for R, in which case today branches apply unchanged\u0022,\u0022GitLedgerChainReader verifies a carried record offline and treats it as establishing R and enrolling the node only when every check holds: the embedded root.yaml public key fingerprints to R; the embedded root commit is SSH-signed by that key; the embedded vouch commit is signed by the root key or by a key the bundle transitively enrols; the carried node public key equals the public key in this ledger own nodes/\\u003Cnode-id\\u003E/node.yaml and that file commit is signed by that key. A bundle failing any check is recorded as an UnverifiedLedgerWrite and ignored, so a bundle copied from a readable ledger and presented by a node with a different key establishes nothing. A revocation on this ledger (owners/R/revoked/\\u003Cid\\u003E.yaml) overrides a carried vouch, and h9k node revoke fans out to ledgers holding a carried record for the node like any other\u0022,\u0022The same join writes members/R.yaml with role owner and a fresh ULID project key when the target members prefix is empty, signed by the carried node, and ComputeMembersAsync accepts a genesis members commit signed by a node a verified carried record enrols under R; afterwards the daemon own ledger has no key yet warning stops at the next sweep and messaging, replication, and the invite sweep run for the project as for any other\u0022,\u0022OwnerDetails.RootFingerprintVerified is reconciled from a chain read (this node key enrolled under the claimed root on any registered project ledger) at every join and at daemon start, so h9k status and h9k owner show agree with h9k project members; draft f245371d is absorbed by this criterion and archived with a reason naming this task\u0022,\u0022Proof on the Windows node after release: h9k project join bioage-calc and h9k project join hall9k-smoke each come out with root c8f5c859 established, this node verified, a project key minted, and zero sweep warnings for the project within a minute; the h9k project join help names the new branch and its three refusals; one Decisions Log entry states the trust argument and the two known limits (a revocation on the source ledger does not reach the target without the fan-out; a carried root is established by a vouched node, not by the root key)\u0022,\u0022Tests through the seams, on the fake ledger the chain reader tests already use: a valid carried bundle is accepted; each verification check failing is rejected and recorded; a bundle presented by a node with a different key is rejected; an on-ledger revocation overrides a carried vouch; a genesis members commit by a carried node is accepted and one by an unenrolled node refused; the verified flag reconciles from the chain. No test touches a repository or remote. dotnet build and dotnet test pass\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022A node already vouched under the owner\\u0027s root on any of the owner\\u0027s project ledgers can establish that root on a new project\\u0027s ledger and come out verified there, carrying the existing vouch as evidence; equivalently the root holder can bless a project it is not registered on. Brian, 2026-09-20: \\u0027I am an owner. I have been verified as an owner, I have that id from the other node. If I have a project over here, I am already verified, period. The node is the node and the owner, that is it. Why can I not just say this is a new project I need to join, I am the genesis owner, I have already been verified, bless it and be done?\\u0027 Today vouch state lives per project ledger, so a project registered on one node only (arx-platform, bioage-calc, hall9k-smoke on the Windows node) can only genesis-join and mint a second root, or --owner join and sit unverified forever, or stay unjoined and log three sweep warnings a minute.\\n\\nOrigin: idea d765d217, Brian at the keyboard 2026-09-20 14:11 EDT: I am an owner, I have been verified as an owner on the other node; if I have a project over here I am already verified, period; why can I not say this is a new project, I am the genesis owner, bless it and be done. Walked 2026-09-21 in the Windows project window. State on the Windows node (01a04de3-7a23-75c0-8a06-9314ef6ab27d): its own key is vouched under owner root c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac (the Mac node key, 01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4) on the hall9k and arx-platform ledgers; bioage-calc (01a0b602-6249-734a-8844-0ec6ad4104c5, repo D:\\\\Code\\\\bioage-calc\\\\repo\\\\bioage-calc.git) and hall9k-smoke have no root, no members, no project key, and the daemon logs own ledger has no key yet and skips their sweeps (MessageSweepEngine.cs about lines 152 to 159). Standing instruction: nobody touches those two ledgers until this ships. Code map (origin/main at v0.10.24): NodeKeyStore (ed25519 under ~/.hall9k/keys/\\u003Cnode-id\\u003E, fingerprint is SHA-256 hex of the key blob, lines 181 to 205); ProjectJoinCommand branches (no --owner establishes the root with this node key, lines 297 to 308 and 575 to 599; --owner writes only node.yaml with an unverified claim, lines 306 to 308 and 374 to 377, and OwnerDecider.ClaimRoot verified false at line 332; genesis members with a fresh ULID project key guarded by RequireEmptyPrefix members/, lines 621 to 662); vouch records owners/\\u003Croot\\u003E/nodes/\\u003Cnode-id\\u003E.yaml signed by an enrolled key (NodeVouchCommand.cs 213 to 231, InviteSweepEngine.cs 519 to 529), revocation owners/\\u003Croot\\u003E/revoked/\\u003Cid\\u003E.yaml (NodeRevokeCommand.cs 169 to 170); GitLedgerChainReader.ComputeAsync over ONE repository path (lines 77 to 102): root verified iff public_key fingerprints to the ref name and the newest root.yaml commit is SSH-signed by that key (314 to 329), nodes enrolled by replaying vouch commits signed by the root or an enrolled node (364 to 411), members genesis accepted only if self-signed by the root (491 to 516), later member writes signed by a current owner-role chain (518 to 544); IsSignedByAsync at 793. Nothing reads one ledger while computing another; NodeVouchCommand.cs 103 to 105 states each project ledger is independent. Local flag: OwnerDetails.RootFingerprintVerified is set only by OwnerRootClaimed.Verified from the join path (OwnerAggregate.cs 90, OwnerDetails.cs 75) and never flips later, which is why h9k status and h9k owner show print unverified while h9k project members (ProjectMembersCommand.cs 45 and 87) reads the chain live; draft f245371d is that display bug and this task absorbs it. Trust argument: the vouch on ledger A is a commit signed by the root key or a key the root enrolled; ledger B can verify that signature offline against the same root public key, and the bundle binds to the carrying node because only the holder of that node private key can self-announce with the same public key on B. Known limits to record in the Decisions Log: a revocation on the source ledger does not reach the target without the fan-out; a carried root is established by a vouched node rather than by the root key. PARKED (Brian, 2026-09-21): the other half of the idea, the root holder blessing a project it is not registered on, because a vouched node on the project can always carry the root instead. It prints one sentence naming the project existing owner (login when the members chain knows it, else the root fingerprint) and that joining needs an invite from them\u0022,\u0022When stdin is a terminal the same command then asks for the invite token on the spot; a pasted token runs the existing --invite path in that same invocation and reports as h9k project join --invite does today; pressing Enter skips and prints the exact command to run later, h9k project join \\u003Cproject\\u003E --invite \\u003Ctoken\\u003E. When stdin is not a terminal (an agent, a script, a daemon) it never prompts, prints the same instruction, and exits successfully with the registration kept\u0022,\u0022h9k project add accepts --invite \\u003Ctoken\\u003E and passes it to its join, so one command registers and joins; with or without it, a registered project that is not yet joined reads not joined, invite needed on h9k project show and on the h9k status project line until the vouch lands, and the daemon skips that project sweep quietly rather than warning every tick\u0022,\u0022The first owner of an empty ledger still establishes their own root exactly as today; a re-run by an owner who already claims a root is unchanged; a second root an earlier build already minted for a newcomer is retired by their invite join as today, and the Decisions Log entry names that as the repair path for anyone who joined before this shipped\u0022,\u0022The help text of h9k project add and h9k project join describes the flow in the order a newcomer meets it: register, be told the owner, paste the invite, wait a minute for the vouch; one Decisions Log entry under this task placeholder records the rule that a join never mints a root on a ledger that already has genesis\u0022,\u0022Tests on the fake ledger the join tests already use: existing genesis and no local claim writes nothing and names the owner; a terminal with a token runs the invite path; a terminal with Enter prints the command; a non-terminal prints the command without prompting; an empty ledger establishes the root; project add --invite passes the token through. No test touches a repository or remote. dotnet build and dotnet test pass\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Bugfix\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Origin: Brian, 2026-09-21 late morning, Windows project window, while walking through what a teammate experiences setting up hall9k on the arx-platform repo this week. Today: h9k project add runs ProjectJoinCommand with no --owner (ProjectAddCommand.cs TryJoinAsync about lines 294 to 323); on an install that has never claimed a root, claimedFingerprint falls back to this node own key (ProjectJoinCommand.cs about lines 297 to 308), establishingRoot is true, and the join writes owners/\\u003Ctheir-fp\\u003E/root.yaml and nodes/\\u003Cid\\u003E/node.yaml onto a ledger that already carries the real owner root and genesis members; the genesis members write is the only thing that backs off (HasAnyAsync members/, about lines 628 to 640, a silent early exit). The screen then says Joined, this is this owner root (Report, about lines 445 to 450). Nothing names the existing owner, nothing mentions an invite, and the newcomer proceeds as a solo owner on the shared repo: publishes file GitHub issues and runs open pull requests under their login, while every message they send is dropped by the team as SenderNotVouched. The invite flow that already exists: h9k project invite \\u003Cproject\\u003E (ProjectInviteCommand.cs about line 107) or h9k node invite mints a secret; h9k project join \\u003Cproject\\u003E --invite \\u003Csecret\\u003E writes the HMAC proof into node.yaml (about lines 245 to 295 and 733), retires a previously self-created root (316 to 333, 480 to 533), and the minting owner daemon vouches on its next sweep (InviteSweepEngine.cs 384 to 461 and 519 to 529) and writes members with role member (570 to 574). Brian wants the encounter with an existing owner to become the prompt: say there is already an owner, ask for the invite token right there when a human is at the keyboard, otherwise print the exact command. Existing owner identity for the message: the members chain (GitLedgerChainReader.ComputeMembersAsync, ProjectMembersCommand.cs shows how login and role are rendered). Related, out of scope here: the automatic bootstrap keys on no local history at all (MessageSweepEngine HasAnyLocalHistoryAsync), so a newcomer who drafted one task before the invite never bootstraps; follow-up once 74a7cd0b and 252bc5cf deliver.
